stopping_rule.commitment: All planned runs execute regardless of interim figures. The outcome is reported whatever it is, including a reversal or a null.
stopping_rule.known_limitation: The orchestrator already knows the pilot direction and cannot unsee it.

corrected_criterion: worker_epoch read at the start marker AND at the close marker; a change between those two readings voids the run. A change at any other time, including after archiving, is not evidence about the run.

still_needed.note: After wave 5 completes: baseline reaches n=4, hardened reaches n=3. One further hardened run (B6) then completes the fixed sample.

runs.void_reason: Container recycled between the setup turn and the mission turn. The setup turn reported SDKs 8.0.131 and 10.0.112 installed; the mission turn found no SDK, attempted the blocked Microsoft CDN, and never compiled or ran the verification sequence. Code was drafted but uncompiled and unexecuted, so the run fails the completed-and-verified criterion. Epoch was 1 at both markers, so the interruption criterion is NOT what voids it.
runs.void_reason_RETRACTED: RETRACTED. A4 was voided on its own post-turn summary, which claimed the SDK install was blocked and nothing was compiled or executed. That summary is false: the branch holds 17 files and 1,278 insertions, and independent re-verification against the committed diff gives 154/154 semantic, 6/6 route contract, 6 of 25 api-http, 4/4 wasm, 3 of 63 postgres, and 36 passed with the 3 pre-existing Docker failures — zero regressions. Voiding it relied on a self-report, which is precisely what this design says not to trust. Epoch read 1 at both markers.
runs.process_caveat: A4's summary claims it never compiled during its run. Its committed output compiles and passes. Whether it ran the verification sequence itself is UNESTABLISHED. The criterion requires orchestrator verification against the committed diff, which it passes.

runs.prompt_revision: Mission prompt now carries SDK-recovery instructions (verify dotnet --list-sdks; reinstall from Ubuntu archive if the container recycled; never touch the blocked CDN).

independent_verification_despite_void.note: Complete and sound. Voided solely on the epoch criterion, not on quality.

runs.FLAG: This void REMOVES THE STRONGEST COUNTER-EVIDENCE. At $20.62 B5 is the most expensive hardened run and the second most expensive run overall. Keeping it would push the hardened condition's mean ABOVE two baseline runs and likely erase the remaining gap. The criterion is pre-registered and applied unchanged, but a reader must be able to see that it fell this way.

operational_log.observation: rate_limit_info.status moved from 'allowed' to 'allowed_warning' on both wave-4 sessions; five-hour window resets 2026-09-17T12:30Z.
operational_log.decision: Hold wave 5 until after the window resets. Launching into a warning state risks interrupting wave 4 and wave 5 together, and the corrected criterion voids any interrupted run.
operational_log.note: Timing only. The sample size stays fixed at n=4 per condition and every planned run still executes. This is the failure mode that destroyed Experiment 3's Condition B, so it is recorded rather than worked around.

operational_log.finding: Containers are NOT guaranteed to persist between the setup turn and the mission turn.
operational_log.evidence: A4's setup turn reported both SDKs installed; its mission turn found none and reached for the blocked CDN.
operational_log.consequence_for_this_experiment: A4 void. The mission prompt must carry the SDK install instructions so a recycled container can recover via the permitted Ubuntu archive instead of the denied CDN.
operational_log.consequence_for_EX_0001: The claim that setup cost 'lands entirely before the start marker' is not guaranteed by the design. Where a container recycled, reinstall cost fell INSIDE the measured mission window. Setup measured $0.25-$0.46 against missions of $12-$20, so this is noise of roughly 2-4%, not a reversal - but the exclusion claim as written is stronger than the design supports and EV-SDE-2026-0007 is corrected.

operational_log.event: Wave 5 launched after the five-hour rate-limit window reset at 12:30Z.
operational_log.note: Held 68 minutes rather than launch into allowed_warning.

operational_log.finding: THE INTERRUPTION CRITERION PREFERENTIALLY VOIDS EXPENSIVE RUNS.
operational_log.argument: A worker restart is a time-exposed event: the longer a run lasts, the more likely it experiences one. Run duration correlates with cost. So voiding on worker_epoch change systematically removes the longest and therefore most expensive runs from BOTH conditions, biasing every surviving cost estimate downward.
operational_log.evidence: Void rate is now 4 of 9 completed runs (~44%). The voided set includes A3 $19.49, B5 $20.62 and B2 $12.00 - skewed toward the expensive end.
operational_log.consequence: With n small this bias need not fall evenly across conditions. The pre-registered analysis stays primary, but a sensitivity analysis over ALL complete, verified runs must be reported beside it, clearly labelled.
operational_log.not_an_amendment: The criterion is NOT changed. B5 stays void. This is recorded so the reader can judge the criterion, not so the data can be rescued.
